html.p: These chart types are well-suited for visualising correlations, density patterns, and multi-dimensional distributions directly from Splunk search results.
A scatter chart plots two numeric fields as (x, y) coordinates. To bind two columns to a single series, use the bracket syntax in seriesDataIndexBinding:
This maps column 1 and column 2 of each result row as a two-element array [x, y] per data point. The search below generates 60 random (x, y) pairs using makeresults and streamstats:

pre.code: | makeresults count=60 | streamstats count | eval x = (random() % 100) | eval y = (random() % 100) | fields count x y

html.p: The result table has three columns: count (index 0), x (index 1), y (index 2). Setting seriesDataIndexBinding=[1;2] binds x and y into each scatter point.

search.query: | makeresults count=60 | streamstats count | eval x = (random() % 100) | eval y = (random() % 100) | fields count x y

html.p: Full viz source for the chart above (copy into a <panel> of your own dashboard):

pre.code:
<viz type="visualization_toolbox.hman">
        <search>
          <query>| makeresults count=60
| streamstats count
| eval x = (random() % 100)
| eval y = (random() % 100)
| fields count x y</query>
        </search>
        <option name="visualization_toolbox.hman.dataType">Custom</option>
        <option name="visualization_toolbox.hman.option">
option = {
  title: {
    text: 'Random Scatter — x vs y',
    left: 'center'
  },
  tooltip: {
    trigger: 'item',
    formatter: '({c})'
  },
  xAxis: {
    type: 'value',
    name: 'x',
    nameLocation: 'end',
    scale: true
  },
  yAxis: {
    type: 'value',
    name: 'y',
    nameLocation: 'end',
    scale: true
  },
  series: [
    {
      name: 'Points',
      type: 'scatter',
      symbolSize: 8
    }
  ]
};
        </option>
        <option name="visualization_toolbox.hman.seriesDataIndexBinding">[1;2]</option>
        <option name="height">350</option>
        <option name="refresh.display">progressbar</option>
      </viz>

html.h1: Bubble Chart — encoding a third dimension
html.p: A bubble chart extends scatter by encoding a third variable as the symbol size. Bind three columns using the [1;2;3] syntax so each data point becomes [x, y, size]. Then use a symbolSize callback to scale the bubble radius from the third value:

pre.code:
<option name="visualization_toolbox.hman.seriesDataIndexBinding">[1;2;3]</option>

series: [{
  type: 'scatter',
  symbolSize: function (val) {
    return val[2] / 4;   // val = [x, y, size]
  }
}]

html.p: The search adds a size column (index 3) representing request volume:

pre.code: | makeresults count=40 | streamstats count | eval x = (random() % 90) + 5 | eval y = (random() % 90) + 5 | eval size = (random() % 60) + 20 | fields count x y size

search.query: | makeresults count=40 | streamstats count | eval x = (random() % 90) + 5 | eval y = (random() % 90) + 5 | eval size = (random() % 60) + 20 | fields count x y size

html.p: Full viz source for the chart above (copy into a <panel> of your own dashboard):

pre.code:
<viz type="visualization_toolbox.hman">
        <search>
          <query>| makeresults count=40
| streamstats count
| eval x    = (random() % 90) + 5
| eval y    = (random() % 90) + 5
| eval size = (random() % 60) + 20
| fields count x y size</query>
        </search>
        <option name="visualization_toolbox.hman.dataType">Custom</option>
        <option name="visualization_toolbox.hman.option">
option = {
  title: {
    text: 'Bubble Chart — x, y and size',
    left: 'center'
  },
  tooltip: {
    trigger: 'item',
    formatter: 'x={c[0]}  y={c[1]}  size={c[2]}'
  },
  xAxis: {
    type: 'value',
    name: 'x',
    scale: true
  },
  yAxis: {
    type: 'value',
    name: 'y',
    scale: true
  },
  series: [
    {
      name: 'Requests',
      type: 'scatter',
      symbolSize: function (val) {
        return val[2] / 4;
      },
      itemStyle: {
        opacity: 0.7
      }
    }
  ]
};
        </option>
        <option name="visualization_toolbox.hman.seriesDataIndexBinding">[1;2;3]</option>
        <option name="height">350</option>
        <option name="refresh.display">progressbar</option>
      </viz>

html.p: A cartesian heatmap requires both axes to be 'category' type and a visualMap component to define the colour scale. Data points are [xIndex, yIndex, value] tuples where the indices reference positions in xAxis.data and yAxis.data.

The chart below shows a simulated log-event density by hour of day (x axis) and day of week (y axis). This pattern is typical for operational dashboards: peak volume mid-morning on weekdays, low activity at night and on weekends.
Full viz source for the chart above (copy into a <panel> of your own dashboard):

pre.code:
<viz type="visualization_toolbox.hman">
        <search>
          <query>| makeresults</query>
        </search>
        <option name="visualization_toolbox.hman.dataType">Custom</option>
        <option name="visualization_toolbox.hman.option">
option = {
  title: {
    text: 'Log Event Density — Hour of Day vs Day of Week',
    left: 'center'
  },
  tooltip: {
    position: 'top',
    formatter: '{c} events'
  },
  grid: {
    top: '10%',
    height: '60%'
  },
  xAxis: {
    type: 'category',
    data: ['00:00', '04:00', '08:00', '12:00', '16:00', '20:00'],
    splitArea: { show: true }
  },
  yAxis: {
    type: 'category',
    data: ['Mon', 'Tue', 'Wed', 'Thu', 'Fri', 'Sat', 'Sun'],
    splitArea: { show: true }
  },
  visualMap: {
    min: 0,
    max: 500,
    calculable: true,
    orient: 'horizontal',
    left: 'center',
    bottom: '2%'
  },
  series: [
    {
      name: 'Events',
      type: 'heatmap',
      data: [
        [0,0,5],   [1,0,8],   [2,0,180], [3,0,320], [4,0,250], [5,0,40],
        [0,1,6],   [1,1,10],  [2,1,210], [3,1,380], [4,1,290], [5,1,35],
        [0,2,8],   [1,2,12],  [2,2,230], [3,2,420], [4,2,340], [5,2,45],
        [0,3,9],   [1,3,11],  [2,3,220], [3,3,400], [4,3,310], [5,3,38],
        [0,4,7],   [1,4,9],   [2,4,190], [3,4,360], [4,4,270], [5,4,28],
        [0,5,15],  [1,5,5],   [2,5,20],  [3,5,55],  [4,5,45],  [5,5,80],
        [0,6,20],  [1,6,4],   [2,6,15],  [3,6,40],  [4,6,30],  [5,6,90]
      ],
      label: {
        show: true,
        fontSize: 10
      },
      emphasis: {
        itemStyle: {
          shadowBlur: 10,
          shadowColor: 'rgba(0,0,0,0.5)'
        }
      }
    }
  ]
};
        </option>
        <option name="height">480</option>
        <option name="refresh.display">progressbar</option>
      </viz>
